headline: Tk 7.14cr gold: BGB seizes 3.6kg gold bars in Jashore
summary: Border Guard Bangladesh recovered 31 gold bars from a car heading toward the Benapole border to be smuggled into India.

headline_marked: Mirza Fakhrul: [[Jamaat is a regimented party]] that does not believe in democracy
headline: Mirza Fakhrul: Jamaat is a regimented party that does not believe in democracy
summary: The Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives claims BNP is the only party that has fought for democracy over the last 50 years.
details: Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir stated that Jamaat-e-Islami is a regimented political party that does not believe in democracy.
He made these remarks on Saturday in Munshiganj after visiting the graves of July martyrs Sajal Molla, Riazul Farazi, and Nur Mohammad Dipzol at the North Islampur social graveyard.
Fakhrul emphasized that the BNP does not believe in one-party rule and claims to be the only party that has struggled for democracy for the past 50 years.
He credited late President Ziaur Rahman for establishing multi-party democracy and Begum Khaleda Zia for establishing parliamentary democracy.
The minister also mentioned that Tarique Rahman remained in exile for the establishment of democracy and noted that his party was elected by a two-thirds majority with public support.

These comments follow a statement by Jamaat-e-Islami Amir Shafiqur Rahman on Friday, who accused the current government of attempting to establish one-party rule similar to the previous Awami League administration.
caption:
Mirza Fakhrul slams Jamaat-e-Islami, calling it a "regimented party" that lacks belief in democracy.

Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir stated that Jamaat-e-Islami is a regimented political party that does not believe in democracy.

He made these remarks on Saturday in Munshiganj after visiting the graves of July martyrs Sajal Molla, Riazul Farazi, and Nur Mohammad Dipzol at the North Islampur social graveyard.

Fakhrul emphasized that the BNP does not believe in one-party rule and claims to be the only party that has struggled for democracy for the past 50 years.

He credited late President Ziaur Rahman for establishing multi-party democracy and Begum Khaleda Zia for establishing parliamentary democracy.

The minister also mentioned that Tarique Rahman remained in exile for the establishment of democracy and noted that his party was elected by a two-thirds majority with public support.

These comments follow a statement by Jamaat-e-Islami Amir Shafiqur Rahman on Friday, who accused the current government of attempting to establish one-party rule similar to the previous Awami League administration.
